title: My coworker's fake boyfriend at Thanksgiving
author: Storytime
hook: My coworker invited me to her family's Thanksgiving so I wouldn't be alone. When we walked in, her whole family yelled, finally, we meet the boyfriend.
story: Last year, I'd just moved to a new city for work. I didn't know anyone. My coworker Rosa found out I'd be alone for Thanksgiving and said, come to my grandma's, there's always too much food. I said sure. In the car, she said, okay, one small thing. My family thinks I have a boyfriend. His name is you. I almost jumped out of the car. She said, please, my aunts will set me up with every man in the parish if I'm single. Just smile and eat. So I did. Her uncles grilled me about my job. Her aunts asked when we're getting married. Her little cousin asked if we kiss. I said, only on Sundays. Everyone laughed. Then her grandma, who's ninety-one, pulled me aside in the kitchen. She said, I know you're not her boyfriend. Rosa can't lie. Her ears turn red. Then she squeezed my hand and said, but I've watched you all night. You keep looking at her when she isn't looking. Fix that by Christmas. That was a year ago. Tomorrow, I'm going back to grandma's. As the actual boyfriend. Part two?
caption: grandma knew before we did 🦃 #storytime
sound: a sweet, playful romantic comedy piano at very low volume
why: A coworker's Thanksgiving invite is trending this week, the fake boyfriend trope is irresistible, grandma calling it out is a perfect twist, and it's posted the day before Thanksgiving.

title: The last turkey in the store
author: Storytime
hook: The day before Thanksgiving, a man in a suit and I grabbed the last turkey in the shop at the same time. I let go. Then he showed up at my door.
story: It was the day before Thanksgiving. The supermarket was chaos. Empty shelves. People arguing over the last bag of stuffing. In the frozen aisle, there was one turkey left. I reached for it, and so did a man in a grey suit. We both held on for a second. He looked exhausted. He said, please. I promised my kids. I let go. I figured I'd make pasta. Honestly, I was alone that year anyway, so it didn't matter. The next day, at three in the afternoon, my doorbell rang. It was him. Holding a roasting tray. Half the turkey, carved. Plus stuffing, gravy, and a pie. Behind him were two little girls holding a handwritten sign that said, thank you for our turkey. I asked how he found me. He laughed and said, you live across the street. We moved in two weeks ago. I've seen you walking your dog. He said, my wife passed last year. It's our first Thanksgiving in the new house. The girls wanted to thank you. Then the youngest one said, you should come eat with us. Should I?
caption: I let go of the last turkey 🦃 #storytime
sound: a warm, gentle acoustic melody that builds softly at very low volume
why: Day-before-Thanksgiving grocery chaos is trending right now, the last turkey standoff is instantly relatable, the new-neighbour reveal is heartwarming, and the invite question pulls comments.

title: Sister-in-law's beige dress code
author: Storytime
hook: My sister-in-law sent a dress code for Thanksgiving dinner. Beige only. Last week, I found out why.
story: My sister-in-law, Kendra, is hosting Thanksgiving this year. Two weeks ago, she sent the family a message. Dress code, neutral tones only. Beige, cream, or light grey. No patterns. No exceptions. Everyone thought it was weird, but fine. Kendra loves aesthetics. My husband even bought a beige sweater. Then last week, I was scrolling through Instagram and saw a post from a home decor brand. Holiday campaign coming soon, shot with a real family at a real Thanksgiving table. Featuring creator Kendra. I clicked her profile. She had a paid partnership. The brand was sending a photographer to her house. On Thanksgiving. To shoot their new tableware. With us in it. In matching beige. As unpaid models. Nobody else in the family knows. My mother-in-law thinks the photographer is just a gift Kendra bought for family photos. I asked Kendra about it. She said, it's not a big deal, you'll get free plates. The brand is paying her four thousand dollars. Dinner is tomorrow. My husband wants to show up in a bright red sweater. Should we?
caption: the dress code was a photoshoot 📸 #storytime
sound: a sassy, upbeat beat with a cheeky twist at very low volume
why: Thanksgiving hosting rules are trending, the beige dress code is a funny hook, the secret brand shoot is a satisfying reveal, and the red sweater question invites petty answers.
